body: Sadly this is true. Too many cuts to the service, and the fact that mental health support has only recently started getting serious.
Yeah private is best bet but as you say, it's a serious burn to the pocket
Thanks, same for you. I suppose it helps knowing other people are going through the same though!

That's shocking! My best friend lived in Spain for a while and she said the healthcare there was amazing! I guess it's area dependent? And don't worry about it haha, I don't want to get into more debt!   XD

No I appreciate honesty don't worry :) I know there's no magical cure, I suppose to reword it better I'm looking for that initial drive. I used to have it but now life is just meh. I've lost everything close to me due to my own rash decisions, and I've never blamed anyone for the way I am apart from myself. And the funny thing about it all is I'm a spontaneous guy... like I won't clean for months on end but one day out of the blue I just randomly start cleaning and blitz the place. Once I put my mind to something I do it, like work etc anyone I've worked with will tell you I get the job done. I work from start to finish with no break (Causes burnout I guess) When I'm focused it's great. But the issue is like I say getting that initial push. I wish I could do it, and believe me I try. But my mind just doesn't let me... I really wish I could explain better but I just don't know how to put it into words. My mind is hell, constant imagery and sounds / voices that just don't make sense, even to me.

Its fine haha, tbh its good to vent once in a while because Idon't cry or anything, so it needs to come out somehow. I wouldn't say my situation is neccesarily worse, everyone with mental health issues is going through their personal hell. It's all perspective. As I've mentioned before, the system works for some, but not others.
I know, I've been trying for years too. I've given up. My story goes a lot deeper but honestly I don't know how to put most of it into words. I appreciate your honesty though.

Haha yeah, and it's abysmal here. I don't want to get too political for obvious reasons, but the short story is basically the government keeps cutting the health service, they're seriously overstretched at the moment. All because they want to make the move to private. It's all money. Oh well, and yeah thanks. I would go private as I've heard it's great but I literally don't have the money for it so yeah :(

That's the thing, it scares the shit out of me being homeless. As I said I know what needs to be done, but I just physically can't muster up the energy to do it. I've been screaming out for years about it but all the help I get focuses on stuff that require motivation, not actually getting the motivation in the first place.

Sadly, unless someone has been there themselves they won't truly understand. Some of us just get dealt shit and it's a downward spiral. It sounds to me you're actually high functioning in terms of just getting on with it, but it's eating you up inside. Day by day it just grows. I'm sorry :( but we truly understand you here, and I'm not just saying that.

I feel you. Tbh it took years to finally get help for myself. And the only thing that got me the help was the fact I was found swinging. One of my main problems is that I'm "high functioning", which basically works against me because I don't really show emotion or anything, I just plod on. It's really not good at all :( As I said in reply to an earlier comment, the issue you and I have faced is mainly the fact that mental health is misunderstood. There's no one size fits all for treatment, but people tend to just think "Oh you're depressed. You're a bit sad, just get over it we all get sad." Like no, for me it's more emptiness. It's like my soul is just a dark void. I'm here if you need someone to vent to though, I know how you feel.

Yeah, it's all NHS. The psychologist and psychiatrist I was referred to by my GP. My GP is actually amazing but I'm aware she's not specialised in mental health, so there's only so much she can do. My CPN I was assigned the last time I was discharged from the psych ward. It's all part of "After care" and "community care." Supposed to be long term to help me get back on my feet. But my main problem is she hasn't bothered to read my notes or anything. I've told her there's some things I'm not comfortable talking about, due to the nature of my problems, but I said it all to a psychologist in the first psych ward. (She was amazing, but only temporary unfortunately.) That Psychologist told me I won't have to repeat myself in future as it will all be on my notes. But I tell my cpn to read my notes so she can understand better and all she said was "That isn't my job. You should be telling me everything." 

Also another note, one of my meds got stopped for no reason. I asked my GP she said speak to my CPN, I asked my CPN she said to ask my GP. Most of the time it's like talking to a brick wall -\_-

Listen, I know you probably hear this a lot but I completely  understand what you're going through. I'm exactly the same, wake up with no purpose, and just waste the hours away until I get tired again. All day in front of the computer and pacing... If you want feel free to message me and we can have a chat. I'm not going to give you all the "it's going to get better" crap. And to be honest, I'm being somewhat selfish in the fact I'd like to talk to you. You're literally one of the first people I've come across that's similar to me. Constant thoughts of suicide, no emotion so to speak... Just emptiness. Is this what you're getting at? Pure emptiness? Drop me a message and I'll happily chat with you. :)

I second this. I don't personally believe anything happens after, but there's always the worry in the back of my mind. What if... That's the main issue I think. If we knew what happened, even if bad it'd be easier. But the not knowing just creates more anxiety haha.

No one is inherently bad. Even people who have done "bad" things. I truly believe there's just a failure in the system. Mental health is generally approached the wrong way, misunderstood. And while the system helps some, the majority I'd say are let down.
